content: Brimonidine belongs to a class of drugs known as alpha-adrenergic agonists. It works by decreasing the production of fluid in the eyes. Brimonidine is available as an eye drop solution and is typically administered three times daily into the affected eye(s). It is important to use the drops at evenly spaced intervals, approximately 8 hours apart, and at the same times each day. Follow the instructions on your prescription label carefully, and consult your doctor or pharmacist if you have any questions. Use the medication exactly as prescribed, without increasing or decreasing the dose or frequency. While brimonidine can help manage your condition, it does not cure it. Continue using the drops even if you feel well, and do not stop without consulting your doctor. To properly instill brimonidine eye drops, follow these steps: 1. Wash your hands thoroughly with soap and water. 2. 3. Avoid letting the dropper tip touch your eye or any other surface to maintain cleanliness. 4. Tilt your head back and use your index finger to gently pull down the lower eyelid, creating a small pocket. 5. Hold the dropper close to your eye without touching it, and brace your hand against your face for stability. 6. While looking upward, gently squeeze the dropper to release one drop into the pocket formed by your lower eyelid. Then, release your lower eyelid. 7. Close your eye for 2 to 3 minutes and tilt your head downward as if looking at the floor. Avoid blinking or squeezing your eyelids. 8. 9. Use a tissue to wipe away any excess liquid from your face. 10. If you need to administer more than one drop in the same eye, wait at least 5 minutes before applying the next drop. 11. Replace and tighten the cap on the dropper bottle, but do not rinse or wipe the dropper tip. 12. Wash your hands again to remove any residual medication. This medication may also be prescribed for other uses. Consult your doctor or pharmacist for additional information. Before using brimonidine eye drops, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to brimonidine or any other medications. Do not use brimonidine if you are taking monoamine oxidase (MAO) inhibitors, such as isocarboxazid, phenelzine, selegiline, or tranylcypromine. Provide your doctor with a complete list of all prescription and nonprescription medications, vitamins, supplements, and herbal products you are currently taking or plan to take.g., amitriptyline, nortriptyline), barbiturates (e.g. Your doctor may need to adjust your medication doses or monitor you for potential side effects. If you are using other topical eye medications, administer them either 5 minutes before or 5 minutes after using brimonidine. Inform your doctor if you experience dizziness when standing up, or if you have a history of depression, circulatory disorders (e.g., Raynaud's disease, thromboangiitis obliterans), or conditions affecting blood flow to the heart or brain. Additionally, disclose any history of heart, kidney, or liver disease. If you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding, inform your doctor. Do not breastfeed while using brimonidine. If you become pregnant during treatment, contact your doctor immediately. If you are scheduled for surgery, including dental procedures, inform your doctor or dentist that you are using brimonidine. Be aware that this medication may cause drowsiness and temporary blurred vision after application. Avoid driving or operating machinery until you know how the medication affects you. Discuss the use of alcohol with your doctor, as it can exacerbate the drowsiness caused by brimonidine. If you wear soft contact lenses, remove them before applying the drops and wait at least 15 minutes before reinserting them. If you miss a dose, apply it as soon as you remember. However, if it is almost time for your next dose, skip the missed dose and continue with your regular schedule. Do not apply a double dose to compensate for a missed one. Brimonidine may cause side effects. Notify your doctor if you experience any of the following symptoms, especially if they persist or worsen: Contact your doctor immediately if you experience: Rash Difficulty breathing Seeing specks or flashes of light Blind spots Fainting Dizziness Nausea In the event of a serious side effect, you or your doctor can report it to the FDA's MedWatch Adverse Event Reporting program. Store brimonidine in its original container, tightly closed, and out of reach of children. Keep it at room temperature, away from excessive heat and moisture. Do not store it in the bathroom. Dispose of expired or unused medication properly, and consult your pharmacist for guidance. In case of overdose, contact your local poison control center at 1-800-222-1222. If the individual collapses or is not breathing, call emergency services at 911. Keep all medical appointments while using this medication. Do not share it with others. If you have questions about refilling your prescription, consult your pharmacist. Maintain a written list of all medications, supplements, and vitamins you are taking, and bring it to all medical appointments or in case of emergencies. Brimonidine is sold under the brand name Alphagan P®. Combination products containing brimonidine and timolol are marketed under the brand name Combigan®.
